episodes.title: Contract WS01 · Contract Formation
recap: Shop displays and ordinary adverts are invitations to treat. An advert is an offer only if it's unilateral, and the performer must have known of it.
A counter-offer destroys the original offer, but a mere question leaves it open. An offer can be revoked before acceptance, even if promised open, unless the offeree gave consideration.
A posted acceptance takes effect on posting, but a revocation takes effect only on receipt. The postal rule is lost where the offer requires the acceptance to be received.
A vague key term, or an essential term left to be agreed with no machinery, means no contract. A meaningless subsidiary term is severed. A lock-out needs a definite period and consideration.

episodes.title: DR WS06 · Disclosure and Privilege
recap: An adverse document must always be listed. Privilege or disproportionality can stop only inspection, and harm to the case is never a ground to withhold it.
Intermediate and multi-track claims without personal injury use a disclosure report, then the menu. Fast track and personal injury claims get whatever the court directs.

Not listed means specific disclosure. Listed but refused as disproportionate means specific inspection. For pre-action and non-party disclosure, the respondent generally gets its costs, even though it loses.
Without prejudice offers are never shown on liability, unless there's a concluded settlement or impropriety. And the duty to preserve documents starts once litigation is contemplated.
